basic_identification.full_title: Square Tins — 15 kg/litre for Ghee, Vanaspati, Edible Oils and Bakery Shortenings — Specification (Second Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Production and General Engineering / Metal Containers (approved by the Chemical Division Council and finalized by the Metal Containers Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies requirements for manufacture, dimensions, capacity, construction, and performance testing of new, plain, internally uncoated square tins of nominal capacity 15 kg or 15 litres. These tins are designed specifically for the hygienic packaging, storage, distribution, and transport of ghee, vanaspati, edible oils, bakery fats, and bakery shortenings.

revision_history.edition: Second Revision (revised to optimize constructional details, establish tinplate and tin coating thickness rules, specify lead-free pure tin solder, and update the hydraulic pressure leak test thresholds to align with the Vegetable Oil Products Control Order)

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Drums and Tins (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all 15 kg/litre Square Tins manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India for packaging ghee, vanaspati, edible oils, and bakery shortenings must conform to IS 10325:2000 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Enforcement transitioned for medium and large-scale enterprises on April 17, 2024, small enterprises on July 17, 2024, and micro enterprises on October 17, 2024. Manufacturing, importing, or distributing non-certified tins in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial steel/tin packaging.

requirements.detail: Every certified square tin must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 10325) stenciled, printed, or embossed on the tin body or lid.
The tin coating must conform to Grade E 2.8/2.8 as evaluated by the chemical stripping method of IS 1327, ensuring a uniform protective barrier against corrosion.

The top and bottom end plates must be attached to the body using leak-proof double-seamed joints along with a food-grade seaming compound resistant to fats and oils. The side body seam must be securely welded (welded side seam) or folded and locked.
A carry handle manufactured from steel wire (diameter as specified) must be securely spot-welded or attached to the top end to withstand normal lifting and handling stresses without tearing free.

When intended for packing ghee specifically, the interior of the square tins must be coated with a compatible, non-toxic food-grade lacquer to prevent any off-flavors, rancidity, or chemical reaction.

To guarantee that the tins are completely leak-proof and can withstand handling pressures, representative sample tins must be subjected to an internal hydraulic pressure test of 30 kPa (0.30 kgf/cm²) for a period of not less than 3 minutes. The tins must show zero signs of leakage, sweating, or joint warping.
The interior of each finished square tin must be completely clean, dry, bright, and free from any traces of rust, solder flux, scale, or foreign contaminants before filling.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10325 : 2000 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing square tins of 15 kg or 15-litre capacity used in the food-processing and agricultural sectors for packing, storing, and transporting ghee, vanaspati, edible vegetable oils, and bakery shortenings. Under India's statutory Drums and Tins Quality Control Order (QCO), all such 15 kg square tins manufactured or distributed domestically must conform to this standard and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Crafted from high-quality cold-reduced electrolytic tinplate (0.28 mm single reduced or 0.21 mm double reduced) with an E 2.8/2.8 tin coating, the tins are designed with standard dimensions (235 x 235 x 325 mm) to optimize warehouse stacking. The standard enforces detailed quality requirements, including continuously welded side seams, double-seamed ends, food-grade interior lacquers for ghee, and a mandatory 3-minute hydraulic pressure leak test at 30 kPa to prevent transport oil spills.
